gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune by buying his train ticket in advance.
gaps.explanation: save a fortune means to avoid spending a large amount; buying in advance keeps money.

gaps.sentence: Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: It took him months to ___ the habit of biting his nails.
gaps.explanation: break a habit (or kick a habit) means to stop doing something you do regularly.

gaps.sentence: We are still ___ arrangements for the wedding.
gaps.explanation: make arrangements is the fixed collocation for organising plans.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.
